name: Jeremai
title: One of the men who had taken foreign wives
summary: Jeremai was an Israelite from the sons of Hashum who lived in the period after the return from the Babylonian exile. He was one of the men who had taken foreign (non-Jewish) wives and, during Ezra's reforms, committed to sending them away to preserve the religious purity of the people.

keyEvents.title: Listed among those who took foreign wives
keyEvents.description: Jeremai is mentioned among the sons of Hashum who had taken foreign wives in violation of the Mosaic Law after the return from exile.

keyEvents.title: Ezra's reform movement
keyEvents.description: Under Ezra's leadership, it was revealed that many Israelites, including Jeremai, had married women from surrounding nations, which was considered a serious breach of the covenant.

keyEvents.title: The people's pledge to send away the foreign wives
keyEvents.description: Jeremiah was among the men who made a covenant to send away their foreign wives and thus restore their faithfulness to the Lord.

keyEvents.title: The account of Hasshum's sons
keyEvents.description: The entire group of Hasshum's sons, including Jeremiah, Mattaniah, Shecaniah, Jaddai, Joel, and Benaiah, were specifically named as those who had to repent for their mixed marriages.
